clinicalPearls: Defined by the sudden appearance and/or rapid increase in the number and size of multiple seborrhoeic keratoses, frequently on the trunk in a Christmas-tree distribution.
The eruption is often accompanied by pruritus of the lesions.
Classic associations are gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma (gastric, colorectal) and lymphoproliferative disease, with breast and lung carcinoma also reported.
It frequently coexists with malignant acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms, consistent with a shared growth-factor mechanism.
It remains a debated entity because seborrhoeic keratoses are very common with age; the abrupt eruption is the key discriminating feature.
New eruptive keratoses may be provoked by inflammatory dermatoses such as erythroderma or eczema, which must be excluded before attributing them to malignancy.
Lesions may regress following successful treatment of the underlying tumour.
reference.pathophysiology: The sign of Leser-Trelat is postulated to result from tumour-secreted growth factors, particularly transforming growth factor alpha acting on epidermal growth factor receptors, with possible contributions from epidermal growth factor and other mediators. These stimulate rapid keratinocyte proliferation, producing the eruptive formation of seborrhoeic keratoses. The frequent association with acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms supports a common humoral, growth-factor-mediated pathway. A true paraneoplastic relationship is difficult to prove given the high background prevalence of seborrhoeic keratoses in older adults.
additionalDifferentials: Eruptive keratoses secondary to inflammatory dermatoses or erythroderma
Melanoma or other pigmented lesions mimicking a seborrhoeic keratosis
additionalInvestigations: Age-appropriate cancer screening including upper and lower gastrointestinal evaluation
CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis
Full blood count, blood film and LDH to screen for lymphoproliferative disease
Skin biopsy of a representative lesion to confirm seborrhoeic keratosis and exclude mimics
Faecal occult blood testing and colonoscopy
Mammography and other age- and sex-appropriate screening
redFlags: Genuinely abrupt eruption of numerous seborrhoeic keratoses
Concurrent acanthosis nigricans or tripe palms
Associated weight loss, anaemia or altered bowel habit
Pruritic truncal eruption with systemic symptoms
reference.prognosis: When a true paraneoplastic marker, prognosis follows the underlying malignancy, often gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma or lymphoma; the keratoses themselves are benign and may regress with tumour treatment.
pitfalls: Over-diagnosing the sign given how common seborrhoeic keratoses are with ageing
Not excluding a preceding inflammatory dermatosis as the cause of eruptive lesions
Failing to biopsy and thereby missing a melanoma masquerading as a keratosis
management: Investigate for and treat the underlying malignancy, most often gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma or lymphoproliferative disease, as the definitive intervention
Age- and sex-appropriate cancer screening including upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy and cross-sectional imaging
Exclude inflammatory dermatoses such as erythroderma and eczema that can provoke eruptive seborrhoeic keratoses
Symptomatic relief of pruritus with emollients and antipruritic agents
Destruction of troublesome keratoses by cryotherapy or curettage for symptoms or cosmesis
Monitor the eruption, which may regress with successful treatment of the tumour
Oncology referral and coordinated multidisciplinary care directed at the causative neoplasm
